title: Khao Moo Daeng – Thai Red BBQ Pork with Rice
description: Khao Moo Daeng is a famous Thai street-food dish featuring tender red-charred BBQ pork served over fragrant jasmine rice with a rich sweet-savory red sauce. Traditionally accompanied by Chinese sausage, soft-boiled egg, fresh cucumber, and herbs, this dish balances caramelized pork, umami sauce, and refreshing garnishes for a complete Thai comfort meal.

ingredients.title: For Moo Daeng (Red BBQ Pork)
items: Pork shoulder or pork neck – 1 kg, well-marbled and tender
Shaoxing wine or dry sherry – 2 tbsp
Red food coloring – a drop (optional, for traditional color)

ingredients.title: For Nam Daeng (Red Sauce)
items: Cornstarch slurry – 2 tsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water

ingredients.title: For Jasmine Rice
items: Thai jasmine rice – rinsed well and steamed until fluffy

ingredients.title: For Accompaniments & Garnish
items: Soft-boiled egg – cooked for 6 minutes with slightly runny yolk
Chinese sausage (lap cheong) – steamed and thinly sliced

instruction.title: Step 1 – Preparing Moo Daeng (Red BBQ Pork)
steps: Slice pork into long strips approximately 4 cm thick.
Combine all marinade ingredients and coat the pork thoroughly.
Cover and refrigerate for 6–12 hours to allow the flavors to penetrate.
Roast at 200°C (390°F) for 20 minutes, brushing with marinade every 10 minutes.
Reduce heat to 160°C (320°F) and continue roasting for another 20–25 minutes until caramelized and glossy.
Rest the pork before slicing thinly for serving.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Preparing Nam Daeng (Red Sauce)
steps: Heat pork roasting drippings in a saucepan.
Add stock, oyster sauce, soy sauces, hoisin sauce, palm sugar, tomato paste, and spices.
Simmer for 10–15 minutes until the sauce becomes rich and glossy.
Adjust sweetness and seasoning until balanced.
Add cornstarch slurry to lightly thicken the sauce.
Strain the sauce for a smooth restaurant-style finish.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Preparing the Rice
steps: Cook Thai jasmine rice until soft, fluffy, and aromatic.
Keep the rice warm until ready for plating.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Preparing Accompaniments
steps: Slice fresh cucumber and prepare scallion julienne.
Steam and thinly slice Chinese sausage if using.
Prepare soft-boiled eggs by cooking for 6 minutes, then halving them.
Prepare crispy pork belly slices if adding extra texture.

instruction.title: Step 5 – Restaurant-Style Plating
steps: Shape jasmine rice into a neat dome on the plate.
Arrange Moo Daeng slices over the rice in a fan shape.
Add Chinese sausage slices, crispy pork belly, and half a soft-boiled egg.
Spoon the glossy red sauce generously over the pork while keeping some rice visible.
Garnish with cucumber slices, cilantro, and scallion julienne.
Serve with chili vinegar dipping sauce on the side for extra acidity if desired.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve hot over jasmine rice with plenty of red sauce for the classic Thai street-food experience.
Pair with cucumber slices and fresh herbs to balance the sweetness and richness of the pork.
Add chili vinegar or Nam Jim-style dipping sauce for a spicy and tangy contrast.

chefTips: Charcoal roasting adds authentic smoky flavor; brush the pork with diluted honey during the final minutes for a professional glaze.
Rest the roasted pork before slicing to keep the meat juicy and tender.
The red sauce should be silky and glossy — straining it creates a refined restaurant-quality finish.
Balance is essential: sweet caramelized pork, savory sauce, refreshing cucumber, and fluffy rice should complement each other.
Choose well-marbled pork shoulder or neck for the most tender texture.
